_comment: TWO jobs, TWO dedicated binaries. (1) THE BLUE-REPORT LOCKDOWN. report.md is read-only to every seat EXCEPT the allowlisted author agent_type (frank-exchange-of-views:blue-synthesizer); a response seat changes it only through `feov-record blue edit`. PreToolUse DENIES a non-author raw write (Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit by file_path, or a Bash cp/mv/tee/redirect/sed -i into blue/report.md) WHEN THAT PATH IS INSIDE A LIVE RUN; outside a run it is a no-op, which is what it was always documented to be and was not. PostToolUse BLOCKS and forces a repair if a non-author call dropped a finding-marker by any mechanism (the exotic-Bash backstop the PreToolUse verb-set cannot enumerate). The gate reads agent_type from the hook stdin (present inside subagent tool calls) and decides in-binary. (2) RUN-DIRECTORY INJECTION (#281): when the call is NOT denied and the payload cwd resolves a live-run marker, PreToolUse REWRITES a Bash command that invokes feov-record in command position, prefixing `export FEOV_RUN='<runDir>'; ` — so a seat stops typing an absolute path it can mistype (measured: one typo cost five manifest receipts and produced a false bug report). Deny wins structurally: hookgate.PreOutcome consults the deny arm first and cannot return a rewrite once it fires, because the protocol permits ONE hookSpecificOutput document and a rewrite emitted in a deny's place is a lockdown that silently opened. THE MATCHER IS WIDE AND THE DECISION IS NARROW, because Claude Code matches on TOOL NAME and there is no path predicate at the matcher layer. That trade is only safe while the binary cannot fail, which is why these are DEDICATED SINGLE-PURPOSE BINARIES rather than verbs on feov-record: as `feov-record hook pretooluse` the invocation carried no --seat-id, the identity-scoped surface refused it, and the refusal's exit 2 denied every mutating tool call in the session. The bootstrap guard mirrors prosthetic-conscience: a fresh plugin-cache version ships without binaries (they arrive via doctor --fix), and an unguarded hook would crash-storm every tool call in that window; the guard degrades to ONE stderr line. The decision ALWAYS travels in the stdout JSON with exit 0, enforced at the process boundary by hookcmd.Run rather than documented on a leaf.

hooks.command: B="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/feov-pretooluse"; if [ -x "$B" ] || [ -x "$B.exe" ]; then exec "$B"; fi; echo 'frank-exchange-of-views: hook binaries missing (new plugin version?) — run /prosthetic-conscience:doctor --fix' >&2

B="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/feov-posttooluse"; if [ -x "$B" ] || [ -x "$B.exe" ]; then exec "$B"; fi; echo 'frank-exchange-of-views: hook binaries missing (new plugin version?) — run /prosthetic-conscience:doctor --fix' >&2
